subject: Kinetic AI RFP: Dedicated Reservation / GPU Sizing Questionnaire
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@kinetic.ai>

Cc: procurement@kinetic.ai; Samir Rao <samir@kinetic.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Kinetic RFP - Dedicated capacity questionnaire (initial)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for taking our call last week. As discussed, we've been running an internal RFP for vendors that can support a dedicated inference reservation for our multi-tenant document parsing product. Attached is a short questionnaire focused on practical sizing and commitment planning. High level asks:

- Recommended GPU families for a mix of large-context generation (16k tokens) and medium short-chat (1k tokens) workloads.
- Throughput targets: target 95th percentile token/s and suggested headroom for peaks.
- Reservation phasing: pilot -> scale plan, and fallback/backfill options.

We'd like to get vendor responses by EOD Wed (19 Aug) to feed into procurement scoring. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide conservative ROI numbers (cost per 1M tokens served at both steady-state and peak) and whether you support burst capacity off-reservation?

Thanks — attached is our spreadsheet with workload profiles.

Regards,
Elena Morales
Head of Procurement, Kinetic AI

Attachments: kinetic_workload_profiles.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Subject: Re: Kinetic RFP - Dedicated capacity questionnaire (initial)

Elena —

Appreciate the materials. Looping in Ben (capacity lead) and Kimberly (pricing & contracts) to get a consolidated response. We can absolutely provide a concise sizing recommendation and cost math. Quick clarifications so we target the right slate:

1) Are the 16k-token requests evenly distributed across users, or concentrated in a small subset of heavy jobs? (profile shows a 5% heavy-job tail — confirm)
2) For peak tolerance, are you measuring per-minute token ingress or concurrent requests?

We'll produce a two-page response (technical fit + pricing) and a mutual action plan for pilot -> full reservation. Attachments from our side will include a GPU fitment matrix and a sample reserved pricing term sheet.

Proposed timeline: internal draft Tue morning, send to you Tue afternoon, final by Wed EOD. Does that work?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kinetic RFP - Dedicated capacity questionnaire (technical draft)

Jonas / Kimberly —

I reviewed Kinetic's workload CSV and sketched a recommended GPU mix and throughput assumptions. High-level technical notes below; I'll attach the detailed fitment matrix.

Summary recommendation:
- Base reservation: 16x A10G (or equivalent Ampere FP16 profile) + 4x T4s for embedding/low-latency routing. Rationale: A10G balances 16k-context generation cost and sustained throughput; T4s are cheap for small requests.
- For models that are fully FP16/quantized int8, we can swap some A10G capacity for 8x H100s if they prioritize latency over cost for <50ms p50 targets — but that increases unit cost by ~2.2x.

Throughput & headroom:
- Steady-state target (95th pct): 2.5M tokens/day => ~29 tokens/sec sustained per A10G instance for mixed-length profile.
- Peak headroom recommendation: plan for 2.5x steady-state burst capacity. In practice, this is provided via a combination of pre-provisioned burst lane (reserved spare) + short-term cloud bursting.

Reservation phasing:
- Phase 1 (pilot, 4 weeks): 4x A10G + 2x T4; tooling integration, KV-prefix caching warmup, observe tail latency.
- Phase 2 (scale, 3 months): ramp to 12x A10G + 3x T4; add autoscaling rules with burst guardrails.
- Phase 3 (steady, annual commit): full 16x A10G profile (with optional H100 lane for latency-sensitive models).

Operational callouts:
- We recommend model quantization for lower-cost packing; Redwood Optimize can run a quick eval to show quality delta across 8-bit vs FP16.
- KV cache sizing: prewarm with 48 hours of representative traffic for best hit-rate.

Attachments in my reply: redwood_gpu_fitment_matrix.xlsx (detailed perf numbers + cost per token at different qconfigs).

Ben
Ben Carter | Capacity Strategy Lead, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@kinetic.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai; priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Kinetic RFP response - dedicated reservation sizing & commercial outline

Elena / Samir,

Thanks for the speedy turnaround. Please find our consolidated answers below and attached artifacts. We kept the response focused to match your scoring rubric.

1) Recommended GPU families and sizing
- Primary fit: 16x A10G-class nodes (good balance of 16k-context throughput and unit economics).
- Light-weight inference: 4x T4 (routing, embeddings, low-latency chat).
- Optional low-latency lane: H100s for <50ms p50 requirements (recommended only for a small subset of inference types).

2) Throughput targets and cost math (summary)
- Steady-state (95th pct) throughput target: 2.5M tokens/day. Based on our profiling, that maps to ~0.6 tokens/second per user for your active set and requires the above baseline to keep tail latency under 300ms for medium-length requests.
- Cost per 1M tokens (steady): estimated $15–18 / 1M tokens using FP16 A10G baseline with prefix caching and batching enabled.
- Cost per 1M tokens (peak-burst): estimated $38–45 / 1M tokens when using burst H100 lanes and on-demand capacity. Detailed line-item math in attached pricing sheet.

3) Reservation phasing and runbook
- Pilot (4 weeks): 4x A10G + 2x T4, onboarding support, one live-runbook exercise to validate tail-latency.
- Scale (3 months): incremental increases to full baseline; regular cadence (weekly) telemetry reviews.
- SLA & fallback: we offer a reserved pool with SLA on uptime. If reserved pool utilization spikes above configured thresholds, requests can failover to a lower-cost hosted tier (with rate-limited throughput) or to H100 lane if purchased.

4) Burst and overage handling
- Redwood Dedicated supports limited, contractually-defined burst capacity. We recommend a pre-allocated burst buffer (10% of committed capacity) + the option to buy ad-hoc burst slots.

5) Next steps & mutual action plan
- Today/Tue: tech + pricing Q&A (this thread)
- Wed: final redlined term sheet from Redwood (Kimberly)
- Fri: mutual action plan + pilot kickoff (MW engineering sync)

Attachments: redwood_gpu_fitment_matrix.xlsx; reserved_pricing_term_sheet.pdf; mutual_action_plan_kinetic_redwood.docx

Please confirm whether you'd like us to price an H100-backed low-latency lane in addition to the A10G baseline — we can include a separate line item. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
